caught_by: the agent itself (count sanity: 1 method from 107 scripts)
what: The crawler regex looked only for 'WS_X.asmx/Method' URLs and found 1 web service method.
fix: The scripts call a helper, ajaxProxy(webServiceCarteira, "Method", data). The extractor now parses that helper and resolves the service variable. 424 methods found.

what: The id generator split acronyms wrong: BS2OndeRetirar became bs_2_onde_retirar, ListarPASPercentual lost words.
fix: The generator and the lint now split method names the same way (acronym-aware).

what: Entity references pointed to finders that themselves need an unknown ID (for example ObterDetalhesAtivo for ativoID).
fix: Finders are ranked: a curated list action first (BS2ListAtivos, BS2Init), never a reader that needs an unknown ID.

what: Read actions with Auth, Token or B3 in the name were marked as changing the account.
fix: External effects apply only to writes.

what: The read probe was designed to learn parameter names from ASP.NET 'missing value for parameter' errors. The server hides error details and answers only 'There was an error processing the request.'
fix: Parameters now come from the requests the app itself sends: a logged-in browser opened all 105 BS2 screens and recorded 598 web service calls with their bodies.

what: The flow capture logged the same SalvarMovimentacao call three times, because listeners from two failed browser scripts stayed attached to the page.
fix: The read-back showed one movement. tools/build_catalog.py now drops repeated lines of the same flow, screen, method and body.

caught_by: the agent itself (checked the generated ids)
what: Told the user the static scan had missed the Pesquisar method. It had found it.
fix: Corrected in the next message. Only ListarDiversificacaoPercentualGeral appears in the capture and not in the scripts.

what: The scenario engine returned None for an empty path, so a check on a top-level list always failed.
fix: An empty path now means the whole answer.

caught_by: lint L002 still failing after the fix
what: A text replacement in the generator silently did nothing, because the formatter had reflowed the target code.
fix: The edit was redone on the current file. The lint result is the check that the change took effect. Later code edits assert that their target text exists, and the repo pre-commit hook runs ruff (see C024).

what: Two writes were verified by scenarios but their catalog entries listed no input fields, because the scripts build those bodies in a variable (JSON.stringify(s)). An agent could not know what to send.
fix: The build now takes the input fields from the flow capture and from the bodies of successful scenario calls. Lint L011 fails any observed or verified write without input fields.

caught_by: the agent itself (read the new entry's status)
what: A method found only in the browser capture came out as excluded: the rule 'every script is a site-wide script' is true for an empty list of scripts.
fix: The exclusion rule now needs at least one script. tests/test_discovery.py checks a capture-only method is not excluded.

caught_by: positive control (looked for calls sent with ID 0 after the probe reported zero placeholders)
what: The read probe was meant to mark calls sent with a fake ID (0) as placeholders. The edit never landed, because the formatter had reflowed the target line, so 214 calls had no mark. The build would have counted reads with fake IDs as verified.
fix: The build now decides by itself: a read call counts only if no ID input, other than the session IDs, is 0, empty or null (bastter_exec.placeholder_ids). Code edits now assert their anchor exists.

caught_by: subagent (imovel family), by reading the account after a timeout
what: A Salvar call timed out on the client while the server still created the item. The executor logged nothing for calls without an answer, so the evidence had no trace of a write that happened.
fix: The executor now logs every call that gets no answer, with a note that a write may have run, before it raises. The orphan item was found by a read and deleted.

caught_by: the agent itself (a failed status came from a development run)
what: The build let the last read-back line decide a write's status, so a failed development run could mark a write failed after the final scenario passed, or the reverse.
fix: Only the latest run of each scenario counts. A write is failed if any scenario's latest run fails its read-back, else verified.

caught_by: negative control (repeated a permanent delete on an item already deleted)
what: The executor logged a call as ok when HTTP said 200, even when the answer was {"Error": ...}. The MCP server would have shown a refused write as a success.
fix: A 200 answer with an Error field is now logged as not ok, and run_action returns it as an error with the server's message.

caught_by: agent demo (the MCP refused the agent's first finance entry)
what: Input types inferred from captured bodies ignored null values, so despesaDedutivel only accepted an object and run_action refused the null the app itself sends.
fix: A field the app sends as null in any captured or successful body now accepts null.

caught_by: agent demo (the read-back showed 11 March instead of 3 November)
what: Date fields did not state their format in the catalog entry. Formats change by screen (mm/dd/yyyy, dd/mm/yyyy, yyyy-mm-dd). The demo agent sent dd/mm to a mm/dd field; it caught this in the read-back and fixed the same movement.
fix: catalog/date_formats.yaml holds the format of each date field with its source, and the build writes it into the field description. Lint L012 fails a runnable write whose date field has no stated format.

what: The permanent delete took every successful excluir_item line in the log, including calls made through the MCP server. A real asset the user hid through the agent would have been deleted for good by the next full scenario run.
fix: Only items hidden in runs of a scenario file count. MCP calls now go to an untracked private log.

what: The demo cleanup chose items by ticker (ITSA4) and deleted all their movements. A real ITSA4 holding would have been wiped.
fix: The demo takes a snapshot of the account before the first request, and the cleanup deletes only records that are not in the snapshot, then checks the account matches it.

what: Lines logged before C015 said ok true for answers with an Error field. Two reads were verified without ever returning data, and refused deletes counted as successful hides.
fix: One rule (bastter_exec.succeeded) decides success everywhere: HTTP 200, no error, and no Error field in the answer shape.

what: Thanks and sardinhagem writes were verified with no confirmation, and their schema did not force privado true, so an agent could publish to the community.
fix: Both input schemas pin privado to true, so run_action refuses a public entry.

what: The MCP input check refused 15 bodies that had worked on the live account, because the generator guessed field types from names.
fix: The build retypes each field from the values that worked (union of types, null allowed when sent).

what: 43 of 90 verified writes had no read-back in their entry, while the docs said run_action returns the read-back for each write.
fix: The build takes each write's read-back from the scenario step that proved it (postcondition.from_scenario). Lint L013 fails a verified write without one.

caught_by: ruff F821 during the audit fixes
what: The read probe used httpx without importing it: an import edit had not applied, so its timeout handler would have crashed with NameError on the first timeout.
fix: The import was added. The repo pre-commit hook now runs ruff, which fails on undefined names.

what: Three methods on the never-run list (an integration init, a money-transfer authorization check and a raffle list) were called by the bulk read probe and became verified, because the list lived only in the guide.
fix: The never-run list is now in the generator (tools/gen_catalog.py FORBIDDEN), and every match becomes excluded, reads included. CarteiraExcluir was added later (audit round 2).

caught_by: fresh-context audit round 2 (correctness, safety), shown with an offline simulation
what: After a failed step the scenario engine ran every later delete step. race_meta_excluir and race_periodizacao_excluir take no ID, so a guard that found the owner's real goals would have deleted them.
fix: A failed guard step now stops the run with no cleanup. Otherwise only steps that undo this run's writes run: a step with undoes whose write step was reached, or a delete that uses IDs this run saved.

what: salvar with ativoID 0 returns the existing item for a ticker, even a hidden one. Nine asset scenarios did not check the ticker first, so on an account that held it they would edit and delete the owner's trades, and the purge would delete the item for good.
fix: Each asset scenario now has two guard steps: the tab does not hold the ticker, and the item that salvar returns has no movements.
now_checked_by: tests/test_scenario_engine.py::test_every_scenario_file_follows_the_cleanup_rules (fails when a guard is removed from a scenario) and ::test_a_ticker_add_without_guards_around_it_is_a_problem

what: Two round-1 fixes were too strict: a save that found a real null failed (InsightsClasses), and list_excludes failed on every literal null in where (DataFreio: null), so three scenarios failed with nothing wrong.
fix: A save now fails only on a missing path, or on a null without nullable: true. list_excludes fails only when a ${ref} has no value.

what: The build used only the latest run of each scenario, so a run that stopped early moved every write it never reached back to seen. A read-back that could not run (timeout) marked its write failed.
fix: Verdicts now use, per scenario and per write, the latest run that reached that read-back. A read-back that could not run is logged with passed null and skipped.

what: diario_atividade_salvar feeds a public top 50 and ran with no question, while the README said the agent never runs public writes. A body with privado and Privado could pass the private pin.
fix: run_action refuses every action marked publishes or notifies_people, whatever its status. Keys that differ only in case are refused, and the private entry objects allow only their four known keys.

caught_by: fresh-context audit round 2 (correctness), then the live purge
what: The purge counted any OK delete as done, without the not-found proof. On imóveis the delete answers OK twice and the imóvel still reads back, so the earlier purge runs never deleted them.
fix: An item counts as gone only after a logged call got the not-found Error. Imóveis are skipped, and the 5 hidden ZZTESTE imóveis (41241 to 41245) are listed as a residue.

what: The demo snapshot never expired. A later cleanup run would treat every record the user added since the demo as a demo record and delete it.
fix: The snapshot holds its time. Cleanup refuses a snapshot older than 3 hours or without a time, and deletes it after a clean pass.

caught_by: fresh-context audit round 3 (correctness, docs), shown with offline simulations
what: The C027 guards had a read-back between salvar and the movement guard. If that read-back failed, the cleanup hid (or deleted for good) an item no guard had checked, which could be a hidden asset of the user. The test of the guard put it right after the create, so it never tested the real order.
fix: The movement guard runs right after salvar. No cleanup step runs past a guard that has not run. scenario_problems requires a guard right before and right after every salvar that adds a ticker, and item_ajustes marks its notes check as a guard.

what: The purge deleted for good from an old log line, without reading the item again. The demo cleanup snapshot saw only visible items, so the user's hidden ITSA4 brought back by salvar would have lost its movements.
fix: The purge rereads each item with the tab and movement reads of the run that hid it, and skips it when it is visible or has movements. The demo cleanup removes only records that the demo's own MCP calls created, never deletes an item for good, and reports the rest.

what: Verdicts were keyed by scenario and write, so a later run that stopped after the first read-back of a write hid a failed second read-back of it. equals also passed {X: null} when X was missing.
fix: Read-back lines log the step name and verdicts are keyed by it. equals fails on a missing path.

what: The weight diary feeds a public ranking with logins but was not marked publishes. The scenarios claim counted a file that only mentions postcondition_of in its description.
fix: diario_salvar is marked publishes, so run_action refuses it. The claim counts YAML keys only.

caught_by: fresh-context audit round 4 (safety), confirmed by the false-positive evaluator with a simulation
what: The demo cleanup counted any mcp- run and only the creates. If the demo created and then deleted its own buy on the user's returned ITSA4, the user's movement on it was deleted and the cleanup reported a clean pass.
fix: The demo starts the MCP server with BASTTER_RUN_LABEL=demo, so its runs are mcp-demo-*. The cleanup subtracts the demo's own deletes, requires each new movement to have a quantity the demo sent, and requires the ZZTESTE prefix on entries and categories.

what: The cleanup rules were checked only by the test suite. bastter_exec.py scenario ran a file that broke them against the live account.
fix: scenario() calls scenario_problems first and makes no call when a rule is broken.

what: export_public.py emptied any target folder, so a wrong path (.. or the repository itself) would delete local files. Its ID check used word boundaries and read the IDs from the working tree.
fix: The export refuses this repository, its parents, folders inside it, and non-empty folders that are not a clone of the public repository. IDs come from the committed log (one value each), are replaced next to any non-digit, and are searched as plain bytes in every file and file name.

caught_by: fresh-context audit round 4 (correctness), then a live probe
what: The movement guard and the purge recheck assumed that the movement read with mes 0 and ano 0 lists past years. Every test movement was dated today, so nothing proved it. The purge also skipped the movement check when the hiding run logged no movement read.
fix: acao_ciclo_completo writes a buy dated 01/02/2019, reads it back with its stored date (2 January 2019) and deletes it. The purge treats a missing movement read as unsafe.

what: When a buy could not be deleted in a cleanup (its ID was not saved), the cleanup still hid the item with the buy inside. A failed guard or assert left no log line of its own.
fix: A skipped cleanup step blocks later cleanup steps on the same record. Failed guards and asserts log a check line with the step name.
